stories.title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
stories.author: Linxi "Jim" Fan
bullet_points: Introduces RoboTTT, a method to scale visuomotor context for robot policies up to 8K timesteps.
Achieves this massive context scaling without increasing inference latency, a significant technical hurdle.
Enables new capabilities such as one-shot imitation from video and on-the-fly policy improvement.

stories.title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
stories.author: Linxi "Jim" Fan
bullet_points: Introduces RoboTTT, a new framework for robot policies that significantly scales visuomotor context to 8K timesteps.
Achieves this massive context scaling without increasing inference latency, a major technical hurdle overcome.
Enables advanced capabilities such as one-shot in-context imitation and on-the-fly policy improvement in robotics.

stories.author: neversaydie
bullet_points: Detection of an atmosphere on an Earth-like exoplanet.
The planet is located within the habitable zone of its distant star.
This represents a significant step in the search for extraterrestrial life.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31.
The performance boost is achieved on Apple Silicon using MLX and multi-token prediction (MTP).
Coding agent performance saw up to 90% speedup according to the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these AI agents entirely on local, personal hardware.
It integrates native support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM execution.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, enhancing local AI inference speed.
The feature is currently available in a preview release, indicating active development.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed for local execution.
It integrates messaging apps with local AI coding agents.
The core value proposition is running AI agents entirely on the user's own device for privacy.

stories.title: TikTok is testing an AI likeness detection tool
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: TikTok is piloting an opt-in tool designed to detect and flag AI-generated likenesses on the platform.
Creators can use this new feature to report content they believe is an unauthorized AI likeness.
This development signals a growing industry focus, with YouTube also reportedly developing similar detection technology.

stories.title: Google-backed satellites for wildfire detection launch as smoke chokes US, Canada
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Google-backed FireSat program is launching satellites specifically designed for wildfire detection.
The new satellites possess enhanced capabilities to detect wildfires that existing satellite systems may miss.
The deployment is timely, addressing the severe issue of smoke choking the US and Canada.

stories.title: San Francisco orders Apple, Google to remove nudify apps from app stores
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: San Francisco has mandated that Apple and Google remove 'nudify' applications from their respective app stores.
The action targets apps designed to influence user behavior, suggesting regulatory scrutiny over manipulative design patterns.
The financial implications are significant, with estimates suggesting Google and Apple earned millions from these apps.

stories.title: Pretraining Data Can Be Poisoned through Computational Propaganda
stories.author: Kyle Lo
bullet_points: The research demonstrates that Large Language Models (LLMs) can be poisoned during pretraining using computational propaganda.
This poisoning introduces harmful behaviors into LMs that are challenging to detect and mitigate.
The attack feasibility extends beyond limited, established data sources, addressing gaps in prior research.

stories.title: SceneBind: Binding What and Where Across Vision, Audio and Language
stories.author: Eli Shlizerman
bullet_points: SceneBind introduces an omni-modal representation capable of integrating vision, audio, and language for scene understanding.
It specifically addresses a limitation in existing models by providing explicit 3D spatial structure, moving beyond just instance-level semantics.
The core innovation is representing scenes as semantic-spatial entities using a global embedding combined with object-centric slots.

stories.title: AutoSynthesis: An agentic system for automated meta-analysis
stories.author: Stefan Feuerriegel
bullet_points: Introduces AutoSynthesis, an end-to-end multi-agent system designed for automated meta-analysis.
Addresses the critical bottleneck of manual and non-scalable quantitative evidence synthesis across various fields (science, medicine, policy).
The system automates the entire process, from formulating search strategies based on natural language questions to extracting data from full-text studies.

stories.title: When Words Are Safe But Actions Kill: Probing Physical Danger Beyond Text Safety in Hidden-State Risk Space
stories.author: Ke Xu
bullet_points: Investigates the critical gap between text safety and physical safety when LLMs control embodied agents.
Demonstrates that linguistically safe instructions can lead to dangerous physical outcomes when grounded in the real world.
Uses hidden-state analysis to show that 'content danger' (CD) and 'physical danger' (PD) are separable signals within LLM representations.

stories.title: Pretraining Data Can Be Poisoned through Computational Propaganda
stories.author: Kyle Lo
bullet_points: The research demonstrates that Large Language Models (LLMs) can be poisoned during pretraining using computational propaganda.
Previous poisoning research was limited to small, established datasets like Wikipedia, failing to address large-scale, heterogeneous corpora.
The study highlights the difficulty in detecting and mitigating harmful behaviors introduced by poisoned pretraining data, especially when interacting with data curation pipelines.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces significant performance improvements.
Enhanced GGUF model compatibility is achieved via llama.cpp integration.
The update broadens model support across various hardware, augmenting MLX on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The update also enables web search functionality within the Claude Code environment.
This enhances the capabilities of local LLM orchestration tools like Ollama.

stories.title: Apple’s plot to crush OpenAI
stories.author: David Pierce
bullet_points: Apple is currently engaged in a lawsuit against OpenAI.
The lawsuit's allegations are described as intense, though some experts view them as standard industry practices.
The article aims to analyze Apple's motivations for pursuing this public legal action against OpenAI.

stories.title: Samsung’s redesigned Z Fold 8 with a wide display just leaked
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Leaked images reveal the design of the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8, showing a shorter, wider foldable form factor.
The leak occurred just prior to Samsung's expected July 22nd official launch event.
The leaked visuals also provide initial glimpses into the phone's specifications, including processor details.

stories.title: SciDiagramEdit: Learning to Edit Scientific Diagrams from Paper Revisions
stories.author: Jürgen Schmidhuber
bullet_points: Introduces SciDiagramEdit, a system designed to automate the editing of scientific diagrams in research papers.
The system aims to allow authors to modify figures (relabeling, rearranging, restyling) using natural language instructions.
The challenge addressed is the complexity of scientific figures, which are dense infographics composed of heterogeneous visual elements.

stories.title: Beyond Success Rate: Cost-Aware Evaluation of Offensive and Defensive Security Agents
stories.author: Yaron Singer
bullet_points: The paper proposes a new evaluation metric for security AI agents that incorporates computational cost alongside success rate.
Current security evaluations often overlook the operational cost (inference budget) of AI reasoning steps, tool calls, and queries.
The research tests this cost-aware evaluation on offensive (Cybench) and defensive (Splunk BOTS v1) security challenges.

stories.title: SearchOS-V1: Towards Robust Open-Domain Information-Seeking Agent Collaboration
stories.author: Zhicheng Dou
bullet_points: Introduces SearchOS, a system-level multi-agent framework designed to improve open-domain information seeking.
Addresses a critical limitation in current LLM agents: getting stuck in repetitive search loops when initial queries fail.
Focuses on improving task progress tracking and search budget efficiency in complex, multi-step information retrieval tasks.

stories.title: teLLMe Why (Ain't Nothing but a Jam): Exploratory Causal Analysis of Urban Driving Data
stories.author: Jorge Ortiz
bullet_points: Introduces 'teLLMe,' a new system for exploratory causal analysis of urban driving data.
Addresses the challenge of answering causal questions (e.g., impact of rain on traffic) using purely observational data.
Combines causal structure learning with structured event tables derived from dashcam annotations.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Current LLM tokenizers are fixed based on initial pre-training corpus priorities.
Adding new languages later can lead to inefficient tokenization (more tokens per word), increasing latency and resource use.
The impact of this inefficiency is more critical for compact models compared to large cloud models.

stories.title: Online Neural Space Time Memory for Dynamic Novel View Synthesis
stories.author: Xuan Luo
bullet_points: Addresses the real-time constraint challenge in dynamic novel view synthesis from streaming video.
Identifies the computational bottleneck of traditional Test-Time Training (TTT) due to required gradient-based memory updates.
Proposes an 'Online Neural Space Time Memory' mechanism to balance long-horizon memory needs with real-time performance.

stories.title: Mutable Low-Rank Sketches for Retrain-Free Recommendation
stories.author: Nick Clayton
bullet_points: Addresses the 'embedding staleness' bottleneck in two-stage recommendation systems.
Proposes 'mutable sketches' using a KP-tree to store user preferences efficiently.
Allows for on-the-fly embedding updates as new user ratings arrive, improving prediction accuracy.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Existing LLM tokenizers are fixed based on initial pre-training corpus priorities.
Adding new languages later can lead to inefficient tokenization (more tokens per word), increasing latency and resource usage.
The paper addresses this by proposing an 'In-Place Tokenizer Expansion' to improve efficiency, especially for compact models.

stories.title: NeuronSoup: Evolving Asynchronous, Shared-Neuron Temporal Graphs without Backpropagation
stories.author: Subodh Kalia
bullet_points: Introduces NeuronSoup, a novel neural computation architecture moving away from traditional synchronous processing.
Features asynchronous, delay-mediated signal propagation through a pool of physically shared neurons.
Proposes a mechanism to achieve computation without relying on the standard backpropagation algorithm.

stories.title: BadWAM: When World-Action Models Dream Right but Act Wrong
stories.author: Xinchao Wang
bullet_points: World-Action Models (WAMs) are a new paradigm in embodied control, linking action generation with future world prediction.
The paper introduces 'BadWAM' to challenge the assumption that this coupling inherently leads to robustness and safety.
BadWAM provides a unified framework for modeling and evaluating the fragility of WAMs' predictive capabilities.

stories.title: SciDiagramEdit: Learning to Edit Scientific Diagrams from Paper Revisions
stories.author: Jürgen Schmidhuber
bullet_points: SciDiagramEdit addresses the manual and time-consuming process of editing scientific figures during manuscript revisions.
The system aims to automate figure editing using natural language instructions, a complex task due to the dense, heterogeneous nature of scientific diagrams.
This research tackles the challenge of understanding and manipulating complex visual grammars within scientific infographics.

stories.title: Bridge Evidence: Static Retrieval Utility Does Not Predict Causal Utility in Multi-Step Agentic Search
stories.author: Shubham Chatterjee
bullet_points: Traditional retrieval system evaluation (static usefulness) fails when LLMs act as multi-step search agents.
The utility of a document in agentic search depends on its potential to enable future actions, not just its relevance to the current query.
The research highlights a critical gap between static document retrieval performance and dynamic, multi-turn reasoning capabilities in AI agents.

stories.title: Beyond the Leaderboard: Design Lessons for Trustworthy Multimodal VQA
stories.author: Steven A. Hicks
bullet_points: The research focuses on designing trustworthy and interpretable multimodal Visual Question Answering (VQA) systems for healthcare applications.
The study uses GI endoscopy case studies from MediaEval Medico 2025 to evaluate nine existing systems.
While parameter-efficient adaptation improves performance, it does not guarantee faithful or complete clinical reasoning in AI answers.

stories.title: TikStance: A Multimodal and Hierarchical Dataset for Multi-target Stance Analysis in TikTok Political Conversations
stories.author: Bowen Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces TikStance, a new multimodal and hierarchical dataset specifically for stance analysis on TikTok.
Addresses the gap in computational analysis for political discourse on short-video platforms by integrating audiovisual and conversational data.
The dataset is focused on the 2024 U.S. election cycle, covering political discussions involving major figures.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Current LLM tokenizers are fixed based on initial pre-training corpus priorities.
Adding new languages later can lead to inefficient tokenization (more tokens per word), increasing latency and resource use.
The issue is more critical for compact models, as large models can absorb the overhead due to large embedding matrices.

stories.title: Mask-Aware Policy Gradients for Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Philipp Krähenbühl
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of applying Reinforcement Learning (RL) to Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs).
Identifies a limitation in current methods: ignoring the sequential nature of token unmasking during generation.
Proposes a 'Mask-Aware Policy Gradients' approach to handle the complex decision-making process in MDLM generation.

stories.title: The Isomorphic Labs Drug Design Engine unlocks a new frontier beyond AlphaFold
stories.author: andsoitis
bullet_points: Isomorphic Labs has developed a new drug design engine.
The engine claims to advance beyond the capabilities of AlphaFold.
The announcement suggests a potential shift in computational drug discovery methods.

stories.title: Porting a 128-expert MoE (Gemma-4 26B-A4B) to AWS Inferentia2 — where every rank weighted the wrong experts
stories.author: xbill
bullet_points: The article details a complex engineering challenge: porting a large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model (Gemma-4 26B-A4B) to AWS Inferentia2 hardware.
The core technical difficulties involved a dual-path Feed-Forward Network (FFN), a non-traceable sparse expert loop, and a device-specific output bug.
The story highlights the practical difficulties in deploying advanced AI models, noting discrepancies between hardware implementation and CPU reference tests.

stories.title: My Inferentia port matched its reference token-for-token — and still output garbage
stories.author: xbill
bullet_points: The article discusses the challenges of porting large language models (Gemma-4 31B) to specialized hardware (AWS Inferentia2).
It highlights a specific technical hurdle where a successful tensor-parallel recipe for smaller models fails at larger scales.
The author notes a critical issue where validation checks pass despite the model producing incorrect outputs ('garbage').

stories.title: Porting Gemma-4 12B (the encoder-free multimodal one) to AWS Inferentia2
stories.author: xbill
bullet_points: The article details the process of porting the Gemma-4 12B encoder-free multimodal model to AWS Inferentia2 hardware.
A key technical challenge involved the model's sliding-window attention overflowing the Neuron's fused-attention SBUF.
After implementing three fixes, the model achieved a throughput of approximately 15 tokens per second on a single inf2.8xlarge instance.
